about: Every Technic gear: its kind, its teeth, what it takes an axle by, and where its pitch circle is. Read by src/assembly/mechanism.gd; checked against the catalogue, the parts' own connectors and the OMR's real sets by tools/gears.py (tests/test_gears.py). In the app's axes (+Y up, the part's own frame): an LDraw gear's axis is its z, a turntable's its y. kind: spur; double (a double bevel: meshes as a spur and at right angles); bevel (at right angles only); crown (as a spur, and at right angles to a spur); worm; ring (teeth on the inside of a circle). teeth: as the name says; circle: round the whole circle, for a part of a ring. hole: axle (keyed), round (turns on its axle), none. face: for a mesh at right angles, how far the origin stands beyond the pitch plane, LDU. plane: where the teeth are along the axis from the origin. arc: a part of a ring, the middle of its arc (x y z) and how far either side its teeth go, degrees. stubs: lines in the part a gear turns on (a differential's planet), [x y z, ax ay az, half length]. also: more gears on the same part. size: why the part's box is not its teeth's, which excuses it from the diameter check. turntables: top -> base. driving_rings, ring_carriers, clutch_gears: reach is half the part's length along its axis, or [from, to]; a ring keys to a carrier it overlaps and drives a clutch gear its span reaches engage LDU into. not_gears: Technic parts named with teeth that are not read as gears here, and why.

7557.size: its clutch's hub is wider than its teeth

racks_about: Gear racks, in the app's axes (the part's own frame, +Y up): teeth along x, from and to the first and last tooth's middle as the LDraw file draws them, every one 8 LDU apart (ten teeth to four studs, so racks laid end to end keep their pitch); a pinion's centre stands pitch_line + its pitch radius above the rack's origin, measured on the OMR's sets (docs/MECHANISMS.md, section 12); z is where the teeth are across the rack, [lo, hi]. 2790a's teeth are not drawn from a tooth primitive and were not counted; 18942's pinion was not met in a set.
